Repo /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper. Implement perf findings F2, F7, F13 and F12 from the analyst's report ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/perf-analysis/report.md (read all four entries and the 'Where the time goes' section; they give file:line, measurements and fixes). Branch from `origin/feat/delete-process-route` (PR #445, head 0efea0ae; it deletes the process route and is not merged yet; main is ddc4ca51 with #440 guards and the lane model) as `perf/checker-seam`; the PR will be stacked on feat/delete-process-route (retarget to main when #445 merges; merge commits only, never rebase pushed branches). Files you own: crates/semantic/src/{rpc.rs,checker.rs,on_demand.rs,convert.rs} (and their tests). Another worker edits crates/semantic/src/lib.rs (F5), crates/cli extract.rs and gate_harness.rs: do not touch those.
Findings: F2 give each checker lane its OWN snapshot (the two programs share one snapshot and so share tsrs's per-snapshot registry lock `CheckerRegistry`; measured Chakra 1.18 -> 1.05 s with one createSnapshot per lane, gate-large flat but +0.4-0.5 s CPU: find out WHY CPU rises and fix or bound it; the second snapshot build adds 25-35 ms, overlap it with answering). Keep #440's lane semantics intact: a panic on one lane stops every lane, the arena memory bound, the session-wide write lock for snapshot-building requests, release-on-refusal for BOTH snapshots, deep-file refusal. F7 cold first answer: `warm_up` should build and KEEP a snapshot over the project's dependencies so the first request is a ~13 ms `updateSnapshot` instead of a 38-40 ms `createSnapshot` (measured first answer 158 -> 127 ms; budget 150 ms); measure the memory cost at startup (peak RSS and arena bytes) and make sure the #440 memory bound/stop and the watch gate still hold; the snapshot must be released/replaced correctly across edits. F13 on the on-demand path run the conversion on the checker thread to remove ~5 us/request thread hops (17 ms of a first answer, est. -10-15 ms) without breaking lane isolation or the bounded memory rules. F12 converter allocation churn: symbol references parsed into serde_json::Value just to be sent back (rpc.rs:85-89, :602-604, checker.rs:203: 1.66M allocations/236 MB on Chakra): pass them as opaque raw/borrowed handles; `PropKey::of` (convert.rs:389-407) clones the name and every declaration only to look the key up (1.58M allocations/162 MB): look up by borrowed key (hashbrown raw_entry-style/`Equivalent` or a borrowed key struct) and allocate only on insert. Expected wall gain small (converters idle 50-75%), CPU -5-10% (matters on 2-4 core CI runners): measure allocation counts before/after (counting allocator or dhat in scratch, load-independent) and keep only what shows a gain. Do NOT change the replay fixtures' request text unless you re-record them with the built-in checker and explain.
Correctness: BYTE-IDENTICAL output. Full-content diff (parse JSON, drop `stats`, compare; reuse ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/perf-analysis/same.py, identity.sh and ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/final-perf/ab.sh) of `extract --json --quiet --no-cache` vs a build of origin/feat/delete-process-route on ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large/src and ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/checker-default/chakra-only/src in default and weekly settings (`--load-dependencies --collapse-inherited-props none`); the gate_harness determinism mode (subprocess thread variants 1/2/4, 9 outputs identical), memory gate (650 edits: all answered, none stale, last equals a fresh session's; and `--max-rss-mib 44` bound exercised), first-answer and watch ButtonProps modes (no regression; F7 must improve the first answer), the construct checker lane, `construct:parity`. Tests that fail on base for each behavior change: two lanes with separate snapshots release both on refusal/panic and equal one program's answer (`several_programs_answer_as_one_does` extended), warm-up snapshot is reused/refreshed and released correctly, PropKey borrowed lookup equals the owned key, and deterministic ordering (no sleeps for ordering: use gates).
Timing: another worker shares the machine for the first hours: check `uptime` and only take wall-time A/Bs (5 interleaved runs, medians; first answer rounds of 5) when load average is under 4; otherwise report counts and say so; never claim a wall gain you could not measure. Scratch in ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/perf-seam/ (no /tmp). Rust 1.99.1 toolchain first on PATH (/Users/gabe/.rustup/toolchains/1.99.1-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin; commits need MISE_RUST_VERSION=1.99.1 for the pre-commit hook), outside the sandbox where tests need it, `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile` in the worktree if needed. No new scripts/options/recipes; changeset as fits (patch/minor, `just semver`). Before push: `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `just deny`, `just semver`, `just test-rust`, `just test-checker-lane`, `just test-ts`, `just test-napi`; judge by exit code. Signed commits with trailer `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013R2ytvK9B32ZaSUaSe6aAZ`; `git push origin HEAD:perf/checker-seam` (never --no-verify) and verify with `git ls-remote` that the remote SHA equals HEAD. Do not open the PR, do not poll CI. Final report <= 300 words: per finding what changed and its measured effect, correctness proof, SHAs, what was not verified.

2	
3	Baseline: gate-large 1.42-1.49 s / ~990 MiB; Chakra-only 1.06-1.18 s / ~725 MiB; `--no-checker` 80-97 ms; kept-answer rerun 0.25 / 0.22 s.
4	Scratch (instrumented copy, binaries, profiles, scripts, toggles PHASES, ALLOC_REPORT, METHOD_STATS, SYNTAX_FIX, TAIL_FIX, SEPARATE_SNAPSHOTS, PREWARM_KEY): this directory.
5	Identity: F2-F5 together give canonical JSON identical to head (stats aside) on both fixtures, with and without the checker. Repo gates/tests NOT run (no repo changes made).
6	
7	## Measured end-to-end (F3+F4+F5, interleaved medians of 5)
8	Chakra 1.13 -> 1.03 s (-9%); gate-large 1.46 -> 1.39 s (-5%); rerun 0.23 -> 0.17 s (Chakra), 0.25 -> 0.20 s (gate-large); `--no-checker` -14 ms (-15%). Adding F2: Chakra ~1.00 s, gate-large flat (CPU up).
9	
10	## Where the time goes (phase marks)
11	- Structural pass ~70 ms Chakra / ~92 ms gate-large (`dependency_types::load` 44-66).
12	- Program build 63-82 ms. Answering (checker-bound) 0.89-1.16 s / 1.25-1.42 s.
13	- Tail after last answer 147 / 175 ms: free converters + release snapshot 35-55, SourceSyntax 51-59, apply_props 38-45, write JSON 14-19.
14	- Checker (Chakra): getPropertiesOfType 787 req, 836 ms, 288 MB out (57%); getTypesOfSymbols 232 ms; getTypesOfType 152 ms; handle-table lock 5-7% of checker CPU.
15	- Allocations while answering (Chakra): 26.3 M allocs, 7.8 GB. Peak: 712 MiB resident, 590 MiB mimalloc region vs 324-334 MiB live heap (~45% allocator slack; MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=0 no change).
16	
17	## Ranked findings
18	F1 `--format rdt` with the checker: 2.7 s and ~2.9 GB building output (pipeline/rdt.rs:49-91, extract.rs:76,82). MEASURED gate-large 4.29 s / 3.89 GB, 2.74 s of it formatting a 910 MB string; builds a serde_json::Value per 515k prop occurrences (~3.6k distinct) then to_string_pretty. weekly.py:115 runs this path. Fix: stream typed structs to a BufWriter, render each distinct Arc<ParsedProp> once, keep insertion key order. Est. 2.7 s -> 0.2-0.4 s, peak ~1 GB. Effort M. Prove: cmp rdt output default+weekly, with/without checker. Risk low-medium.
19	F2 Own snapshot per checker lane (rpc.rs:395-440): shared snapshot shares tsrs's per-snapshot registry lock. MEASURED Chakra 1.18 -> 1.05 s; gate-large flat, +0.4-0.5 s CPU (unexplained); RSS +0-20 MiB; 2nd snapshot build +25-35 ms (overlappable). Effort S. Identity done; run several_programs_answer_as_one_does + determinism.
20	F3 Merge allocates/hashes a path for each of 431k union props (types/semantic/syntax.rs:70-81): 47-51 ms of a 51-57 ms phase. Fix: skip props already seen (Arc pointer, only with parent), dedupe file names as &str, keep first-seen order. MEASURED after: ~6 ms. Effort S. Identity done.
21	F4 One map conversion costs 14 ms every run (dependency_types.rs:1168, field :296): `loader.exports.into_iter().collect()` rehashes on one thread. Fix: into_read_only() (O(1)), .iter() at :1085. MEASURED `--no-checker` gate-large 95-97 -> 82 ms, Chakra 80 -> 66-76. Effort S. Identity done.
22	F5 One-shot CLI frees memory and releases the snapshot while you wait (semantic/src/lib.rs:277-279, 384-386): drop converters/interner 18-25 ms, awaited release 11-24 ms, runtime drop ~3 ms. Fix (CLI path only): forget them as extract.rs:91 already does for the output; don't await release. ~35-50 ms. Effort S. Library/session callers must still free.
23	F6 Gate harness lacks mimalloc though the addon has it (examples/gate_harness.rs vs binding/src/lib.rs:18-19): system malloc = 28% of converter CPU in the harness. With mimalloc: first answer 171 -> 158-163 ms; watch ButtonProps p95 173 -> 157-161. Not a product speedup: the gates start measuring what users run. Effort S.
24	F7 Cold first answer: build a snapshot during warm-up (on_demand.rs:287,:444,:590): createSnapshot is 38-40 ms of 158-172 ms (107 ms checker, 17 thread hops, ~40 conversion, 5 structural). MEASURED with a snapshot already built: first request is a 13.6 ms updateSnapshot, first answer 158 -> 127 ms. Fix: warm_up builds and keeps a snapshot over the project's dependencies. Est. -25-30 ms (under the 150 ms budget). Effort M. Prove: watch gate byte comparison vs a fresh session. Risk medium (startup memory not measured).
25	F8 Dependency-index cache is slower than no cache (29-32 MB msgpack): load 24 ms, saves ~14 ms. `--no-checker` 15 runs: Chakra 79.5 ms without vs 88.4 ms warm; gate-large 96-110 vs 107. Fix: lazy/zero-copy load (rkyv), smaller index, or drop; measure on the five corpora (sign unknown). Effort M.
26	F9 Rerun: validate the kept answer while the structural pass runs (kept.rs:282-312, extract.rs:49-56): with F3-F5 in-process ~165 ms, kept::load (read 7.3 MB, re-ask every recorded question) 40-43 ms, strictly after the 64 ms structural pass. Validation needs only the file; check the request key afterwards. Est. -30-40 ms (rerun ~0.13 s). Effort M. Risk low-medium (file edited between check and read).
27	F10 apply_props handles 515k props one by one to place ~3k distinct (types/semantic.rs:543-635): 38-44 ms, only 0.6 ms hashing/compare; rest is string clone + BTreeMap insert per occurrence. Fix: sorted Vec + bulk build, or memo whole components. Est. -10-25 ms. Effort S/M.
28	F11 Start building the checker program while the structural pass runs (extract.rs:49): root files known right after Indexed::build; createSnapshot (63-82 ms) could start 55-80 ms earlier. Est. -40-60 ms. Effort M/L. Risk medium: assert root list byte-equal to today's.
29	F12 Converter allocation churn: symbol references parsed into serde_json::Value just to be sent back (rpc.rs:85-89,:602-604, checker.rs:203): 1.66 M allocs / 236 MB on Chakra (top site). PropKey::of (convert.rs:389-407) clones name and declarations to look up: 1.58 M allocs / 162 MB. Wall gain small (converters idle 50-75%); CPU -5-10% (est.), matters on 2-4 core CI runners. Watch replay fixtures if request text changes. Effort S/M.
30	F13 Thread hops on the on-demand path (checker.rs:202-222,:259-279): ~5 us/request, 17 ms of a first answer. Fix: convert on the checker thread for on-demand. Est. -10-15 ms first answer and watch. Effort M.
31	F14 Binary size: 35.1 MB release with 7.4 MB symbol table (nothing strips; Cargo.toml:104-107). __text 18.6 MB, __const 5.2 MB (probably tsrs lib files: guess), unwind tables 2.6 MB (needed by panic=unwind). `strip = "symbols"` ~ -7 MB (-20%, est.), loses function names in backtraces.
32	F15 Canonical writer serializes each distinct prop twice (interned.rs:204-211,236-243): write stored compact bytes as RawValue. Est. -3-6 ms. Low priority.
33	
34	## Checked and fine
35	Process start 4.6 ms; Indexed::build 9-14 ms; resolve_all 11-13 ms; assemble 1.3-2 ms; targets_of <1 ms; merge memo misses 0.6 ms total over 515k lookups; SourceSyntax parsing itself 5-6 ms wall; merge_file loop 3-4 ms; generic-instantiation tail <2 ms; converter threads not the bound (busy 25-60%). SipHash only in two bounded sets in the binding; no regex anywhere; MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=0 same RSS/time. Checker-side JSON writing and the handle registry are tsrs internals, already recorded in docs.

"""Usage: same.py a.json b.json — byte-compare two canonical outputs with the top-level `stats` set aside."""
import json
import sys


def load(path):
    with open(path, 'rb') as f:
        doc = json.loads(f.read())
    doc.pop('stats', None)
    return json.dumps(doc, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':')).encode()


a, b = load(sys.argv[1]), load(sys.argv[2])
print('IDENTICAL' if a == b else 'DIFFERENT', len(a), len(b))
sys.exit(0 if a == b else 1)
#!/bin/zsh
# Usage: identity.sh — head vs the scratch build with every experiment switched on, both fixtures, canonical JSON.
cd /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/perf-analysis
mkdir -p out
for project in gate-large chakra-only; do
  case $project in
    gate-large) src=../gate-large/src ;;
    chakra-only) src=../checker-default/chakra-only/src ;;
  esac
  bin/caliper-head extract --src $src --json --quiet --no-cache > out/head-$project.json
  SYNTAX_FIX=1 TAIL_FIX=1 SEPARATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 bin/caliper-phases extract --src $src --json --quiet --no-cache > out/fix-$project.json
  SYNTAX_FIX=1 TAIL_FIX=1 SEPARATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 bin/caliper-phases extract --src $src --json --quiet --no-cache --no-checker > out/fixnc-$project.json
  bin/caliper-head extract --src $src --json --quiet --no-cache --no-checker > out/headnc-$project.json
  echo "$project checker: $(python3 -I same.py out/head-$project.json out/fix-$project.json)"
  echo "$project no-checker: $(python3 -I same.py out/headnc-$project.json out/fixnc-$project.json)"
  cmp -s out/head-$project.json out/fix-$project.json && echo "$project raw bytes equal" || echo "$project raw bytes differ (stats?)"
done
#!/bin/zsh
# usage: ab.sh <runs> <label> <extra args...>  — interleaved main vs comb, gate-large and chakra-only; prints wall s and peak RSS MiB
runs=$1; label=$2; shift 2
cd $(dirname $0)
for i in $(seq $runs); do

    for b in main comb; do

    done
  done

content.content:
# target/ file lock, serializing what moon's own scheduler thinks is
# parallel work (confirmed via `Blocking waiting for file lock` in verbose
# output). napi/vite-plugin have no such lock to contend over, so moon
# still orchestrates those directly.
build:
    cargo build --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi
    moon run napi:build vite-plugin:build
    cargo build --release

# Run all tests (Rust, the native binding crate, TypeScript, Python)
test: test-rust test-napi test-ts test-py

# Run Rust tests (via nextest, which doesn't run doctests — paired
# with `cargo test --doc` to cover those too)
test-rust:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked
    cargo test --doc --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi

# The binding crate is excluded from the workspace recipes, so its own unit tests run here.
test-napi:
    cargo nextest run -p caliper-docgen-napi --locked

# Run the Python tests for the scripts (standard library only, no dependencies)
test-py:
    python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'

# Run TypeScript tests
test-ts:
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin test
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-storybook test
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle test

# Compare the Go checker and tsrs on every construct-suite row (run on every tsrs bump; see apps/oracle/construct-suite/README.md)
test-parity:
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:parity

# The checker gates of ADR 0026, with nothing allowed to skip: the golden check, tsrs-against-Go parity, and the construct
# suite through the checker path (the release binary, which links tsrs) held to checker-expectations.json; see
# apps/oracle/construct-suite/README.md.
test-checker-lane:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo build --release --locked -p caliper-docgen
    export REQUIRE_CALIPER_BIN=1 CALIPER_BIN="$PWD/target/release/caliper-docgen"
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:check
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:parity
    CALIPER_SEMANTIC=1 pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:checker
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle exec vitest run tests/construct-checker-lane.test.ts
    # S5's gate on tsrs: generic components instantiated.
    cargo test --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --lib instantiate
    cargo test --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --test instantiate
    # S6's gate on tsrs: a kept snapshot brought up to date, and an edit nobody announced caught loudly.
    cargo test --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --test watch
    # The built-in checker's stack holds a type 10,000 deep without aborting its host (trail 369): release only.
    cargo test --release --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --lib a_type_nested_ten_thousand_deep -- --ignored --exact checker::tests::a_type_nested_ten_thousand_deep_is_printed_in_full

# Build the native binding and run the Vite plugin against it
test-integration:
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-napi build:napi
    NAPI_BINARY_REQUIRED=true pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin test:integration
    NAPI_BINARY_REQUIRED=true pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-storybook test:integration

# Measure ADR 0026's memory, determinism, first-answer and watch gates on the built-in checker, as the addon runs it
# (docs/gate-measurements.md). Builds the large project outside the repository (GATE_FIXTURES, default
# ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large), so it needs the network or a warm pnpm store; `just gate-measure --runs 3`
# passes options to every gate. Takes minutes, runs every gate, and fails if any failed.
gate-measure *args:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    fixtures="${GATE_FIXTURES:-$HOME/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large}"
    node scripts/gate_fixtures.mjs "$fixtures"
    cargo build --release --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --example gate_harness
    failed=0
    for gate in memory determinism first-answer watch; do
        target/release/examples/gate_harness "$gate" --src "$fixtures/src" --tsc built-in {{ args }} || failed=1
    done
    exit "$failed"

# The deterministic construct suite on the release binary: goldens current, then the suite, which must not skip
test-construct:
    cargo build --release -p caliper-docgen --locked
    CALIPER_BIN="$PWD/target/release/caliper-docgen" pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:check
    CALIPER_BIN="$PWD/target/release/caliper-docgen" REQUIRE_CALIPER_BIN=1 pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle test

# Pack the npm packages and check napi arrives only as vite-plugin's transitive dependency (pm: npm or pnpm)
verify-install pm="pnpm":
    scripts/verify-install.sh {{ pm }}

# Rust and TypeScript line coverage; with a threshold, fails if either is below it
coverage threshold="": (coverage-rust threshold) (coverage-ts threshold)

# Rust coverage: writes lcov.info and prints the summary before enforcing the threshold
coverage-rust threshold="":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked --lcov --output-path lcov.info
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only
    if [[ -n "{{ threshold }}" ]]; then
      cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{ threshold }}"
    fi

# TypeScript coverage: prints the summaries and writes each package's coverage/lcov.info
coverage-ts threshold="":
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin exec vitest run --coverage {{ if threshold != "" { "--coverage.thresholds.lines=" + threshold } else { "" } }}
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-storybook exec vitest run --coverage {{ if threshold != "" { "--coverage.thresholds.lines=" + threshold } else { "" } }}

# Documentation build check (warnings, including broken intra-doc links,
# treated as errors)
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi

# Unused-dependency check
machete:
    cargo machete

ts_src := "'packages/vite-plugin/src/**/*.ts' 'packages/vite-plugin/tests/**/*.ts' 'packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/storybook/src/**/*.ts' 'packages/storybook/tests/**/*.ts' 'packages/storybook/*.config.ts' 'packages/napi/*.d.ts' 'packages/cli/bin/**/*.js' 'apps/oracle/src/**/*.ts' 'apps/oracle/tests/**/*.ts'"
ts_src_only := "'packages/vite-plugin/src' 'packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/storybook/src' 'packages/storybook/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/napi/*.d.ts' 'packages/cli/bin/**/*.js' 'apps/oracle/src'"
ts_tests_only := "'packages/vite-plugin/tests' 'packages/storybook/tests' 'apps/oracle/tests'"
md_src := "'**/*.md' '!node_modules/**' '!target/**' '!dist/**'"

# Lint and format check
lint:
    cargo fmt --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
    node scripts/check-packaging.mjs
    pnpm exec oxfmt --check {{ts_src}}
    pnpm exec oxfmt --check {{md_src}}
    pnpm exec oxlint {{ts_src_only}}
    pnpm exec oxlint -A pedantic -A perf -A style -A unicorn/consistent-function-scoping -A vitest/require-mock-type-parameters --vitest-plugin {{ts_tests_only}}

# Format code
fmt:
    cargo fmt
    pnpm exec oxfmt {{ts_src}}
    pnpm exec oxfmt {{md_src}}

# Check licenses, advisories, and banned crates
deny:
    cargo deny check

# Check for typos
typos:
    typos

# Lint GitHub Actions workflows for permission, credential, and supply-chain
# issues. --strict-collection fails on a workflow it cannot parse instead of
# skipping it, so a malformed file can never pass by being ignored.
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Everything the moon-managed pre-commit hook runs. `.moon/workspace.yml`
# calls this recipe rather than repeating the commands, so the hook and
# `just ci` can't drift apart.
pre-commit:
    cargo fmt --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
    typos
    cargo deny check

# Everything the CI jobs run, minus the Node version matrix and verify-install
ci: lint test deny typos zizmor doc-check machete semver msrv (coverage "90")

content.content:
crates/semantic/src/rpc.rs:273:    /// Every call and its answer, when the caller asked to record a replay fixture; shared with a layered snapshot.
docs/gate-measurements.md:32:- **Where the time goes.** One answer is about 4,400 requests to tsrs, one at a time: the props of `ButtonProps` are mostly Chakra's style props, each a distinct instantiated union (1,800 `getTypesOfType`, 1,250 `getTypeArguments`, 600 `typeToString`, 560 `batchRequests`, and 43 ms for the snapshot). A request takes about 70 µs, round trip included. Three changes were tried and not kept: converting 16 props at once (360 to 390 ms, but it changes which type handle first asks about a symbol, so the replay fixtures no longer match and would need recording again), batching the requests a level of the walk will make (no faster, so the cost is in the answering, not the round trips) and one documentation batch per component (5%). What would meet 150 ms is fewer requests per component, for example expanding a dependency's instantiated aliases on demand; that is converter work beyond S4.
docs/gate-measurements.md:38:- **What changed.** The client keeps an answer's `result` as text and the backend parses it once, into the type it expects (`Client::request_raw`). A type's members and type arguments are kept by type handle for the snapshot, as the checker's text, so a type converted again asks for neither again. One answer is now 4,593 requests. Output is byte-identical: the whole-program checker run on `gate-large` (938 components) gave the same bytes on main and the branch in 10 runs; the construct suite and checker lane pass; the replay fixtures were recorded again against the pinned tsrs, since the request set shrank.
docs/gate-measurements.md:41:- **Floors, measured.** The branch's 4,593 requests of one answer replayed in order against a fresh tsrs, every answer equal to the logged one: one at a time 348 ms; all of them in 32 batches, so with no round trip left, 162 ms. Add the 40 to 45 ms snapshot and the parse, and an answer of this request set costs about 230 ms however it is batched, prefetched or pipelined. Pipelining does not help either: 1,137 `getTypesOfType` sent at once over one connection took 96 ms, against 86 ms one at a time and 33 ms in one batch, and requests that depend on an earlier answer cannot be sent ahead (with `--async`, tsrs answers out of order, so a handle from an earlier request may not be registered yet).
docs/performance.md:40:- **Fixed in #136: 497 ms and 1.3 GB became 255 ms and 0.3 GB.** Most of the cost was `keyof` walks resolving every member's type when only the names are read, and memo replays copying each recording's diagnostics into every component.
docs/performance.md:110:`PipelineOptions::load_dependencies` defaults to `true` (the CLI, the config file, the Vite plugin, the NAPI binding and the addon; the addon already did). `--no-load-dependencies` turns it off, `--load-dependencies` still means the default, and a project with no packages installed loads nothing either way. It was off while Chakra took 497 ms and 1.3 GB with it on, against 43 ms and 82 MiB without; memo replay, `keyof` name walks, interned keys and a parallel lib parse (#136, #175, #177, #178, #182) took that to about 220 ms and 330 MiB. Five parity corpora, `extract --json`, best of 7, interleaved, on a laptop shared with other jobs (about ±10 ms), off → on:
docs/type-checker-integration.md:75:- **Tests:** `crates/semantic/tests/resolve.rs` runs the backend end to end against the built-in checker (the `markers` fixture project for names and parameters, `tsrs_real.rs` for the error type), and asserts a checker that does not answer in time as the structural output plus one warning. Until trail 369 slice 4 these tests replayed recordings of the Go checker through a fake `tsc` process; with the checker linked in, they ask it directly, and parity with the Go checker is `construct:parity`'s (`apps/oracle/construct-suite/README.md`). The CLI test asserts the default output has no `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` diagnostic.

#!/bin/zsh
# Usage: run.sh <binary> <project gl|ch> <out.json> [extra args...] — one extract, JSON to <out.json>, stderr to <out.json>.err,
# then prints the ALLOC lines and /usr/bin/time's real/user/sys/peak RSS.
cd /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures
bin=$1; project=$2; out=$3; shift 3
case $project in
  gl) src=gate-large/src ;;
  ch) src=checker-default/chakra-only/src ;;
esac
{ /usr/bin/time -l perf-seam/bin/$bin extract --src $src --json --quiet --no-cache "$@" > $out } 2> $out.err
grep ALLOC $out.err
awk '/real/ {printf "real=%s user=%s sys=%s ", $1, $3, $5} /maximum resident/ {printf "rssMiB=%d\n", $1/1048576}' $out.err

/// A diagnostic the checker reports for a file: where it starts and what it says.

content.content:
1	//! Where each of a component's props is declared and what its JSDoc says, from the checker: the interface each of its
2	//! declarations sits in (`parent`, `declarations`), its description and its tags.
3	//!
4	//! A property symbol names the symbol it is a member of (`parent`); one a mapped type or an intersection made
5	//! (`Omit<Base, "x">`, `A & B`) names none, and its declarations are asked for the symbols they declare, whose parent
6	//! is the interface that wrote them. A declaration names its file the way the checker keys files, lower-cased where file
7	//! names are not case-sensitive; the file is reported as the program read it (`getSourceFileNames`), so
8	//! `parent.fileName` is the path on disk, as the structural pass reports it.
9	//!
10	//! Every answer is kept for the snapshot, keyed by what it depends on: a declaration's symbol by the declaration, a
11	//! parent's name by the parent, and a prop's JSDoc by its declarations, which is where the checker reads it, so the
12	//! props a library's components share (an instantiation or an `Omit` makes a new symbol for each) are asked about once.
13	
14	use std::collections::BTreeMap;
15	use std::sync::{Mutex, PoisonError};
16	
17	use caliper_docgen_core::types::PropParent;
18	use rustc_hash::FxHashMap;
19	use serde_json::{Value, json};
20	use tokio::sync::OnceCell;
21	
22	use crate::convert::declared_in;
23	use crate::rpc::{CallError, CompactSymbol, JsDocTag, Rpc, SymbolInfo, decode, flag};
24	
25	/// One prop to look up, and which of its JSDoc to ask for.
26	pub(crate) struct Asked<'a> {
27	    pub(crate) property: &'a SymbolInfo,
28	    /// Ask for its description: the structural pass has none for it.
29	    pub(crate) description: bool,
30	    /// Ask for its tags.
31	    pub(crate) tags: bool,
32	}
33	
34	/// What the checker says about where one prop is declared.
35	#[derive(Debug, Default)]
36	pub(crate) struct Declared {
37	    /// Empty when not asked for, or when it has none.
38	    pub(crate) description: String,
39	    /// Empty when not asked for, or when it has none.
40	    pub(crate) tags: BTreeMap<String, String>,
41	    pub(crate) parent: Option<PropParent>,
42	    pub(crate) declarations: Vec<PropParent>,
43	}
44	
45	/// The symbol a declaration declares, by the parent it names and the reference that asks about it.
46	type DeclaredSymbol = Option<(Option<CompactSymbol>, Value)>;
47	
48	/// What one snapshot's answers about declarations are kept as: they do not change inside it.
49	#[derive(Debug, Default)]
50	pub(crate) struct Memo {
51	    descriptions: Mutex<FxHashMap<String, String>>,
52	    tags: Mutex<FxHashMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>>,
53	    /// By the declaration handle.
54	    symbols: Mutex<FxHashMap<String, DeclaredSymbol>>,
55	    /// A parent symbol's name when it is an interface, else `None` (a type literal, a class, a module).
56	    parents: Mutex<FxHashMap<CompactSymbol, Option<String>>>,
57	    /// The program's files by the path a declaration names: the path itself, and lower-cased.
58	    files: OnceCell<FxHashMap<String, String>>,
59	}

On an app wrapping the 938 components of Chakra UI and MUI it takes 1.8 s instead of 6.2 s, and 1.4 s instead of 5.7 s for the 787 Chakra components alone; `react-docgen-typescript` takes 7.3 s and 4.1 s on the same files. Peak memory is about 10% higher (1.1 GiB instead of 0.98 on that app; 1.5 GiB on three copies of it). The Storybook session keeps asking one program.

perf(semantic): keep symbol references as text and look kept props up by borrowed key

A symbol's reference is only ever sent back to the checker, so it is kept as
the JSON text it arrived as (`SymbolRef`) and written into the request as it
is, instead of being parsed into a `serde_json::Value` and serialized again.
Request parameters are written straight to bytes from small typed structs
(`Asking`), the method name is a `&'static str` end to end, and a name the
checker did not escape is not copied again.

`PropKey` now borrows the property it names; a prop already kept is found
without copying its name, declarations and parent, and only one that is not
kept is copied, into the owned `KeptKey`.

On the 787 Chakra components (`extract --json --no-cache`), allocations on
the converter threads fall from 23.1-23.3 M (6.4 GB) to 8.77 M (4.66 GB);
the checker threads' are unchanged. Output is byte-identical (stats aside).

#!/bin/zsh
# Usage: sample.sh <binary> <project gl|ch> <label> — runs one extract and samples it with `sample` (1 ms) for its
# lifetime; writes prof/<label>.txt.
cd /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures
mkdir -p perf-seam/prof
bin=$1; project=$2; label=$3
case $project in
  gl) src=gate-large/src ;;
  ch) src=checker-default/chakra-only/src ;;
esac
perf-seam/bin/$bin extract --src $src --json --quiet --no-cache > /dev/null &
pid=$!
/usr/bin/sample $pid 5 1 -mayDie -file perf-seam/prof/$label.txt > /dev/null 2>&1

docs/type-checker-integration.md:95:- **Its own threads.** `crates/semantic/src/checker.rs` creates a `tsrs_api::Session` on a thread of its own with a 512 MiB stack, the stack the `tsrs` binary serves on: a query runs on the calling thread, and a type 2,000 deep overflows a default 2 MiB thread, which aborts the process. Requests from any thread reach it over a channel and are answered one at a time; a whole-project `extract` starts a second thread with a channel (a lane) of its own and asks a snapshot of two programs over the same root files, each program's requests down its own lane (`tsrs_api` locks a program's one checker for the length of a request, so two programs are what can be answered at once). Every program holds every root file, so either answers a component as one program would; the Storybook session asks one; `Session::handle_request` is the dispatcher the `tsrs` binary serves, so `rpc.rs` sends the methods and JSON of `tsc --api`. A stack overflow aborts and cannot be caught (deep-type tests: 2,000 levels in every run, 10,000 in release).

perf(semantic): give each checker lane a snapshot of its own, derived from the first

The two programs of a whole-project run shared one snapshot, and with it
`tsrs_api`'s per-snapshot handle registry (`CheckerRegistry`), whose one lock
both lanes waited on. Each lane now asks a snapshot of its own. The first is
built from the disk; the others are derived from it with `updateSnapshot` and
`createPrograms`, so they read every file from the first snapshot's cache, as
the first read it.

Why a second `createSnapshot` raised CPU time: the parse cache spares only
parsing; a fresh snapshot repeats the file system work of a program build.
Sampled on gate-large, `open` went from 400 to 628 samples, `lstat` from 209
to 387 and `stat` from 79 to 118; system CPU rose 0.15-0.2 s a run and the
program build from 78-90 ms to 112-113 ms. The derived snapshot builds in
82-86 ms in all (78-90 before) and does not raise system CPU (1.26-1.42 s
against 1.58-1.61 s).

`Rpc::release` on the first lane releases every lane's snapshot; a lane whose
snapshot cannot be made releases the ones made before it. Output is
byte-identical on gate-large (stats aside).

content.content:
A long-lived session (the Storybook addon, the lazy `WatchSession`) attaches a warm checker instead of running the whole-project pass above (ADR 0022): a napi session does unless `checker: false`. `caliper-docgen-semantic` keeps one checker warm behind a worker thread, answers from a program rooted at only the requested component's file, and returns its props. The program's snapshot is kept between requests and brought up to date with the files the session says changed ("Watch", below). `WatchSession::component` merges them into the structural answer by name (the checker's type wins, a structural prop the checker did not return stays, and `htmlAttributes` applies once after the merge, as in the structural pass) when they arrive within `semanticWaitMs` (default 150 ms), or within `semanticWaitEmptyMs` (default 2,000 ms, never less than `semanticWaitMs`) when the structural answer lists no props at all (a `ComponentProps<typeof Button>` of a package the structural pass does not model, whose props type it could not expand); otherwise it returns the structural answer plus an `Info` diagnostic, and the checker's late answer serves the next request of the same component while no source file has changed. A kept answer carries what the checker said about the request that made it (a warning that it was not told about an edit, why a component kept its structural result), and every request it serves reports that again, a late answer's included; only an unavailable checker's warning is said once per session. There is one request in flight per component key and content hash of its file: a caller that asks while it is in flight (a story asked while its own prefetch runs, or two stories of one component) waits for that answer, so the checker answers it once. The checker answers interactive requests (`WatchSession::component`, `components`) before background ones (`components_in_background`, which `sessionWarmUp`, the addon's `warmUp` and `fillAfter` use, and which waits for nobody), first come first served within each; an interactive caller that joins a background request raises it, and after 4 interactive answers in a row while background requests wait, the oldest of them goes next. Any source-file change, including a file the component only imports, drops every checker answer, so the next request asks again; an answer still in flight at that moment is neither kept nor joined. The component's structural diagnostics that the checker's props supersede are dropped when they replace the structural ones, except while a structural prop the checker did not return is still opaque: those diagnostics name the component, not the prop, so they stay until nothing they could be about is left. (The whole-project merge drops unreturned structural props, so it has no such case.) Which ones are superseded is in "Diagnostics a checker answer supersedes".

Measured with `crates/semantic/examples/ondemand_bench.rs` (50 random components, TypeScript 7.1.0-beta): the first answer takes 82 to 137 ms (Chakra 703 ms), a component asked for alone 21 to 41 ms (Chakra 534 ms), and 2 to 9 ms when asked for in batches of 8 to 32. Where the structural pass is behind (shadcn) the checker reports 2.3 times the props; where it is not (Mantine, Chakra, Spectrum) it reports the same count. The in-memory cache, the 64-program replacement and the failure modes are in the ADR. (These numbers were measured over the `tsc --api` pipe, before the checker was linked in.)

Hardening of the on-demand checker:

- **Versions:** the checker is the pinned `tsrs` crates; nothing is read from the project.
- **Memory** (trail 369 slice 2): after the first request and every fourth, once the reply is sent, the worker reads what the checker holds and compares it with `OnDemandConfig::max_rss_mib` (768 MiB). The bound is between requests: one request that needs more finishes first. This process's resident memory is the host's as well (Node, Storybook, and Caliper's own answers, which grow by about 5.5 MiB per Chakra component asked), so what is read is the resident part of the one address range `tsrs` carves its arenas from (`mincore`, about 6 ms). Past the bound the checker stops for the session: every later request keeps the structural answer, with a `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` warning that names the bound. It is never replaced, because a fresh session does not lower what this process holds: a closed session gives back part of its arenas (Chakra's 46 MiB fell to 22 to 37), and the fresh one parses every file again. Measured on Chakra (`docs/gate-measurements.md`): 650 edits peak at 377 MiB never replaced against 514 MiB replaced every 64 programs, and the arenas stay at 46 MiB over 2,000 edits and reach 165 MiB over 937 Chakra and MUI components. The range is the process's, so it covers every program and lane of the session; the bound is applied by the Storybook session's warm checker (one lane), and stopping it stops all of it. A whole-project `extract` (two lanes) has no bound: it ends with its process.
- **Start and stop:** creating the checker and `warm_up` return at once, and dropping the checker waits at most `shutdown_wait` (5 s) for a request in progress before letting the worker finish alone. The checker's thread finishes a request in progress, then closes its session and exits.
- **Tests:** `crates/semantic/tests/on_demand.rs` asks the built-in checker.
- **Latency, re-measured** (`ondemand_bench`, 30 components, release build, `7.1.0-beta`): shadcn first answer 84 ms, median 21 ms, p90 37 ms; antd first 93 ms, median 36 ms, p90 40 ms. The memory check does not add to a story's wait.

perf(semantic): the warm-up keeps a snapshot over the project's dependencies

`OnDemand::warm_up` started the checker but built nothing, so the first
request paid for a `createSnapshot` that read the lib and every dependency's
declarations from the disk. The warm-up now builds a program rooted at a file
held in the checker's memory (never on disk) that imports each package the
nearest `package.json` lists under `dependencies` and `peerDependencies`,
stamps its files, and keeps it as the live snapshot. The first request brings
it up to date with `updateSnapshot`, re-rooted at its own files and with
announced edits read again; the warm snapshot is then released. An edit
nobody announced is caught as for any kept snapshot, and the memory bound is
checked after the warm-up too.

gate-large (Chakra and MUI, load 7-9): the warm-up takes 63-77 ms; its arenas
hold 38 MiB, and 49-50 MiB after the first answer instead of 40 (peak RSS
20-35 MiB higher). ChakraButton's first answer: gate harness 167 -> 144 ms,
the checker alone 146-156 -> 126-149 ms.

perf(semantic): convert on-demand answers on the checker's thread

An on-demand answer made about 3,200 requests (Chakra's `Button`), each
crossing a channel from the worker to the checker's thread and a oneshot
back. The worker now runs the conversion on the checker's own thread
(`Client::run_on_thread`), in a runtime of its own there, where each request
is answered in place.

The lane's guards hold for requests asked in place: a panic in the session
ends the lane as one in a queued request does (the request fails with it,
later ones fail as to a stopped checker, the session is closed once); each
request is bounded by the caller's deadline, after which the caller stops
waiting with a timeout that names the request and the work's later requests
fail, a release excepted; a panic in the conversion itself leaves the session
answering. The whole-project run is unchanged.

gate harness on gate-large (load 6-9): ChakraButton's first answer 145 ->
115 ms (with the warm-up; 165-173 ms on the base); `watch` (ButtonProps, 100
edits) edit-and-query p50 152 -> 119 ms, p95 156 -> 127 ms, CPU per edit
186 -> 153 ms, peak RSS 452 -> 403 MiB, still equal to a fresh session's.

# Usage: identity.sh <base> <head> — extract --json --quiet --no-cache of both binaries on gate-large and chakra-only, in the

done

---

cargo/caliper-docgen: patch
cargo/caliper-docgen-napi: patch
npm/caliper-docgen: patch
npm/caliper-docgen-napi: patch

---

The built-in checker is guarded so that it does not take Storybook or the CLI down with it. A panic inside it fails only the request that caused it; the session it unwound through is closed and a fresh one answers the next request (after three, the checker stays off for the session, as for a crashed process). A file nested more than 20,000 brackets deep is not given to it, since `tsrs` overflows its parse stack and aborts the process at a few hundred thousand: the components that read it keep their structural answer with a warning naming the file. Its memory is now bounded: past 768 MiB of its own arenas (which leave out the host's memory) it stops for the session and components keep their structural answer with a warning that says why. It is no longer replaced after 64 programs, which raised its memory instead of lowering it (Chakra over 650 edits: 377 MiB peak against 514).
